column2: Leaving aside the feeling of a mother, why do you behave otherwise?
She told him, "You are not my son; Kalashambara stole you, the son of Vishnu.
Thrown into the sea, you reached the belly of a fish, and I obtained you from it; your mother, still very affectionate, weeps for you."
Thus told, Pradyumna challenged Shambara to battle; his mind agitated with anger, the mighty one fought.
Having killed that Daitya's entire army, Madhava's son crossed over seven illusions and joined the eighth illusion.
With that illusion he killed that Daitya Kalashambara, rose into the sky with her and came to his father's city.
Descending in the inner apartments with Mayavati, the wives of Krishna were glad at seeing him; and Rukmini, the blameless, her eyes fixed, said lovingly:

Blessed surely is she whose son this is, newly youthful; if my son Pradyumna were living, he would be of this age.
brahmapuran:200:22	Fortunate is the mother, dear, who is adorned by you; or such is my affection and such your body; clearly you are Hari's child, dear.
In the meantime Narada arrived with Krishna and, delighted, said to the queen of the inner apartments, Rukmini:

This is your son, fair-browed, who has come back after killing Shambara, by whom he was stolen from the lying-in room before.
brahmapuran:200:25	This Mayavati is the wife of your son, virtuous; she is not Shambara's wife; hear the reason here.
brahmapuran:200:26	When Manmatha was destroyed, she, devoted to his rebirth, bewildered Shambara by an illusory form, Rukmini.
brahmapuran:200:27	In marriage and the enjoyments she showed that Daitya a lovely illusory form. She of intoxicating eyes is Rati, the beloved of Kama who descended as your son.
brahmapuran:200:28	There should be no doubt here; this is your fair daughter-in-law. Then Rukmini and Keshava were filled with joy, and the whole city said "Well done, well done."
Seeing Rukmini joined with her son long lost, all the people in Dvaravati then felt wonder.
Bala was defeated by Rukmin for a thousand nishkas; on the second day he was defeated by Rukmin for another thousand.
Then Rukmin, the best of dice-players, took a stake of ten thousand nishkas, which Balabhadra had accepted.
Then the lord of the Kalingas laughed at Bala, Brahmins, showing his teeth; and the fool Rukmin, intoxicated with pride, said:
This Balabhadra is ignorant of the great game and has been defeated, who foolishly thought himself expert in dice out of pride in dice.
Seeing the Kalinga king showing his teeth and Rukmin speaking ill words, Halayudha grew angry.
Then, his mind seized by anger, Halayudha took up a stake of ten million nishkas, and Rukmin then threw the dice.
Baladeva won; he then said loudly, "I have won"; Rukmin said loudly, "No, mine! Enough of false speaking, Bala.
This stake spoken by you is true, but not accepted by me; if you say so, how have you won and not I?"
Then a loud voice in the sky, deep-sounding, increasing the anger of the great-souled Baladeva, said:
Baladeva has won; Rukmin has spoken falsely. Not having said a word, it is done by action.
Then Bala rose up, his eyes red with anger, and the mighty one killed Rukmin with the dice-board.
Seizing the Kalinga king who struggled by force, Bala in anger broke the teeth with which he had laughed openly.
Pulling out a great golden pillar, Bala angrily struck the kings who were of his party.
Then there was a cry of alarm, Brahmins, all of them intent on flight; the whole circle of kings did so when Bala was angry.
Hearing Rukmin killed by Bala, Madhusudana said nothing, from fear of Rukmini and Bala.
Then, taking Aniruddha, whose wedding had been done, the circle of the Yadus with Keshava came to Dvaraka, best of Brahmins.

Kamsa, Kuvalayapida, Putana the child-killer, and all others who were afflictions to the world were brought to destruction by you.
brahmapuran:202:6	In the three worlds protected by the knowledge of your arms, the dwellers in heaven attain satiety by eating the sacrificial oblation at sacrifices.
brahmapuran:202:7	The reason for which I have come now, Janardana — hearing that, you ought to make an effort to remedy it.
brahmapuran:202:8	This Bhauma, named Naraka, lord of Pragjyotisha city, destroys all beings, subduer of foes.
brahmapuran:202:9	Having killed gods, Siddhas, Asuras and kings, Janardana, that Asura imprisoned maidens in his own house.
brahmapuran:202:10	He took the water-streaming umbrella of Varuna and the peak of Mandara, the jewel mountain;
brahmapuran:202:11	that Asura took my mother's divine, nectar-flowing earrings, and wants Aditi's elephant Airavata.
brahmapuran:202:12	This misconduct of his, Govinda, has been told by me to you; what is to be done about it, think yourself.
Hearing this, smiling, the revered son of Devaki took Vasava (Indra) by the hand and rose from his excellent seat.
Mounting the sky-going Garuda as soon as thought, and placing Satyabhama on him, he went to Pragjyotisha city.
Shakra, mounting the elephant Airavata, then cheerfully went to the abode of the thirty as the dwellers of Dvaraka looked on.
Around this city of Pragjyotisha for a hundred yojanas was set a fearful net of snares to ward off enemy armies.
Hari cut those nooses, hurling the discus Sudarshana; then Mura rose up, and Keshava killed him.
Then Hari reduced Mura's seven thousand sons to moths burnt by the fire of the discus's edge.
Having killed Mura, Hayagriva and Panchajana, Brahmins, the wise one quickly rushed upon Pragjyotisha city.
There a battle with a great army occurred between Naraka and Krishna, in which Govinda killed Daityas by thousands.
Hurling the discus, the discus-bearer, destroyer of the Daitya hosts, cut Bhauma Naraka, the mighty, who was showering weapons and missiles, in two.
When Naraka was killed, Earth took Aditi's earrings and approached the Lord of the world, and said these words:

When I was lifted up by you in the boar form, lord, a son born of your touch was born to me then.
brahmapuran:202:24	He was given to me by you and felled by you; take these two earrings and protect his offspring.
brahmapuran:202:25	For the removal of the burden of the earth, the revered one has come to the world with a part of himself, gracious-faced, lord.
brahmapuran:202:26	You are maker, unmaker, destroyer, the imperishable origin, whose form is the world; what can I do in praising you, Achyuta?
brahmapuran:202:27	Pervading, the pervaded, the action, the doer and the deed, the revered one always, the Self of all beings — what is my praise of you, Achyuta?
brahmapuran:202:28	You are the Supreme Self, the Self, the self of beings, the imperishable; when it is so, there is no praise; why should it proceed?
brahmapuran:202:29	Be gracious, Self of all beings; what was done by Naraka, may it be forgiven, for the removal of fault; my son has been felled.
Saying "So be it" to the earth, the revered lord of beings took the jewels from Naraka's dwelling, best of sages.
In the maidens' quarters, that one of incomparable valour saw sixteen thousand maidens and a hundred more, Brahmins.
He saw six thousand fierce four-tusked elephants and twenty-one niyutas of Kamboja horses.
Those maidens, those elephants and horses, Govinda sent to Dvaraka city at once by Naraka's servants.
He saw Varuna's umbrella and the jewel mountain too; Hari placed it on Garuda, lord of birds.
Krishna himself, mounting, with Satyabhama as companion, went to the abode of the thirty to give Aditi the earrings.

Leader of mind, intellect and senses, whose nature is the qualities, free of all conceptions such as white and long,
brahmapuran:203:8	untouched by birth and the rest, free of dream and the like, twilight, night, day, earth, sky, wind and water,
brahmapuran:203:9	fire, mind, intellect, the origin of beings — you are these, Achyuta; you are the doer of creation, preservation and destruction, the lord of doers.
brahmapuran:203:10	By your self-forms named Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, the Lord, by your illusions this world of moving and unmoving is pervaded.
brahmapuran:203:11	The knowledge of the self in the non-self is that maya of yours, Janardana, by which the feeling 'I' and 'mine' arises here.
brahmapuran:203:12	In the midst of worldly existence this is your doing, lord, of your maya: the men by whom you are worshipped intent on their own duty,
brahmapuran:203:13	they cross all this maya for self-liberation. Brahma and all the gods, humans and likewise animals,
brahmapuran:203:14	enveloped in the blind darkness of delusion in the great whirlpool of Vishnu's maya, worshipping you desire desires, for the exhaustion of their own becoming.
brahmapuran:203:15	By your maya, revered one, men are bound at your feet; I, desiring a son and the destruction of the enemy side,
brahmapuran:203:16	worshipped you not for liberation; that is the play of maya. A desire, almost like covering a loincloth, even from the wishing tree,
brahmapuran:203:17	arises in the unmeritorious; that is an offence born of one's own fault. So be gracious, imperishable creator of the delusion of the maya of the whole world.
brahmapuran:203:18	Destroy ignorance, you who are the existence of knowledge, lord of the beings of beings. Salutation to you with discus in hand, salutation to you with the Sharnga bow in hand,
brahmapuran:203:19	Vishnu with mace in hand, salutation to you with conch in hand. I see this your form adorned with gross marks; I do not know your highest; be gracious, Supreme Lord.
Aditi, thus praised, Vishnu smilingly said to the mother of gods:
Goddess, you are our mother; be gracious, be the giver of boons.
So be it, as you wish; you, tiger among men, will be unconquerable by all gods and Asuras in the mortal world.
Immediately after this, Satyabhama bowed to Diti, accompanied by Shachi, and said again and again, "Be gracious."
By my grace, fair-browed, you will have neither old age nor ugliness; blameless-limbed, you will have all desires.
The king of gods, permitted by Aditi, duly worshipped Janardana with great honour.
Then Krishna, with Satyabhama as companion, saw all the gods' gardens such as Nandana, good ones.
He saw the fragrant Parijata, bearing clusters of blossoms, giving cool delight, divine, adorned with copper-red shoots,
born at the churning of nectar, radiant as gold, Lord of the world Keshava, killer of Keshi; seeing it, Satyabhama said to Govinda, best of Brahmins:

Why is this tree not taken to Dvaraka, Krishna? If your word is true, that I am especially dear to you as Satyabhama,
brahmapuran:203:30	let this tree be taken to my house for the garden; neither Jambavati nor Rukmini is as wished by me.
brahmapuran:203:31	'As you are, Satya,' you have said repeatedly to me, Krishna; if that is true, Govinda, and not a courtesy-speech,
brahmapuran:203:32	then let this Parijata be the adornment of my house; I wish to shine among my co-wives bearing a bunch of Parijata blossoms in my hair.
Thus told, Hari, laughing, placed the Parijata on Garuda; the forest-guards said to him:

O Shachi is the queen of the king of gods, and the Parijata is her property; Govinda, you should not take the tree.
brahmapuran:203:35	It was brought forth by the gods at the churning of nectar for adorning Shachi; you will not depart in safety taking it.
brahmapuran:203:36	From folly you ask for it; who would go in safety taking it? Surely, Krishna, the lord of the gods will take offence.
brahmapuran:203:37	With the thunderbolt in hand Shakra, followed by the immortals — enough of fighting with all the gods, Achyuta. The wise do not praise an act bitter in result.
Thus told, Satyabhama, very angry, said to them:

What is Shachi to the Parijata, or who is Shakra, lord of gods? If it arose at the churning of nectar as common to all worlds,
brahmapuran:203:40	why does Vasava alone take it, forest-guards? As gods, the moon and Shri are common, so the Parijata tree is common to all the world.
brahmapuran:203:41	Out of great pride in her husband's arm, Shachi obstructs it. So go quickly and tell Paulomi my word; Satyabhama says so, in words haughty with pride in her husband:
brahmapuran:203:42	'If you are your husband's beloved, if you are dear to him, then have my husband's taking of the tree prevented.
brahmapuran:203:43	I know your husband Shakra, I know the lord of the thirty; yet I, a mortal woman, have taken this Parijata from you.'
Thus told, the guards went and said aloud what was said; Shachi urged her husband, the lord of the thirty.
Then Indra, surrounded by the armies of all the gods, proceeded to fight Hari for the Parijata, Brahmins.
Then the gods were ready with clubs, swords, maces, spears and weapons, when Shakra stood with thunderbolt in hand.
Then Govinda, seeing Shakra seated on the king of elephants, with the divine retinue, standing ready for battle,
blew his conch, filling the directions with the sound, and released a shower of arrows numbering a thousand ten thousand.
Then seeing the directions and sky covered with hundreds of arrows, all the gods released weapons and missiles in many ways.
Each missile and weapon released by the gods, thousands, the Lord Madhusudana, lord of worlds, cut in sport.
The Garuda-eater (Hari), drawing the noose of the lord of waters, cut it in pieces as if it were the body of a young serpent.
The staff sent by Yama, broken by a mace-throw, the revered son of Devaki felled on the earth.
He ground the palanquin of the lord of wealth to sesame-bits with the discus; Shauri made Sun and Moon lose their power by a glance.
Agni was struck by hundreds of arrows, the Vasus put to flight in all directions, and Rudras with spear-tips cut off by the discus were felled on earth.
Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, Maruts and Gandharvas, driven by Sharngin's arrows, all flew in the sky like silk-cotton fluff.
Garuda too devoured with his mouth, wings and claws, striking gods and Danavas; always the bird.
Then Devendra and Madhusudana rained on each other thousands of arrows, like two clouds with streams.
In that crowd Garuda fought with Airavata, and Janardana fought with Shakra among the assembled gods.
When weapons and missiles had been cut and scattered, Vasava quickly took the thunderbolt and Krishna the discus Sudarshana.
Then a cry of alarm arose in the three worlds with the moving and unmoving, seeing Indra and Janardana holding thunderbolt and discus.
The thunderbolt thrown by Indra was caught by the revered Hari, who did not release the discus then, saying, "Stay, stay."
Satyabhama said to Devendra, whose thunderbolt was lost and whose mount was wounded by Garuda, intent on flight:

It is not fitting, lord of the three worlds, for Shachi's husband to flee; Shachi will wait on you with a garland of Parijata.
brahmapuran:203:64	What kind of kingdom is it for you, god, if Shachi comes lovingly and you do not see her radiant with the garland of Parijata as before?
brahmapuran:203:65	Enough of effort, Shakra; you ought not to feel shame. Let this Parijata be taken; let the gods be free of pain.
brahmapuran:203:66	Shachi, in the pride of her husband, with great honour did not see me, who had come to her house, with proper hospitality.
brahmapuran:203:67	Being a woman, I, with a light mind, intent on praising my own husband, therefore fought with you, Shakra.
brahmapuran:203:68	Enough of the Parijata taken from another's property; what woman is not proud of beauty and fame?
Thus told, the king of gods turned back, Brahmins; he said to her, "Enough, angry friend, of this great grief.
I feel no shame at being defeated by him who is the creator, preserver and destroyer of all, in his universal form.

In whom this whole world, with no beginning or middle, is, from whom and by whom it will not be, from the being of all beings: how can there be shame, goddess, for one cast aside by that cause of origin, dissolution and preservation?

The form of all worlds, small and very subtle, is known by the knowers of all the Vedas, not by others; who can conquer him, unborn, uncreated, the Lord, eternal, who by his own will is the primal cause for the welfare of the world?"

Whatever you are, you are, lord of the world; you stand in the course of activity, Lord; you remove the world's thorn, destroyer of Asuras.
brahmapuran:204:7	Let this Parijata be taken to Dvaraka city, Krishna; once released by you in the mortal world, it will not stay on earth.
Saying "So be it" to the lord of gods, Hari came to earth, praised by Siddhas and Gandharvas, urged on by the sages.
Krishna quickly went, taking the best of trees; then blowing the conch, he stood above Dvaraka.
He produced joy in the residents of Dvaraka, Brahmins; descending from Garuda with Satyabhama as companion,
he placed the great tree Parijata in the garden; approaching which all the people remember their former birth.
The fragrance of whose flowers perfumes the earth for three yojanas. Then all those Yadavas saw divine scents, non-human,
on that tree, as it showed them its face. The wealth of elephants, horses and the rest was brought by servants.
Krishna took the women from Naraka's household; then at an auspicious time Janardana married.
Those maidens who had been brought from Naraka's house on all sides, Govinda, at one time, best of Brahmins,
took their hands by rule, in separate bodies, according to his dharma: sixteen thousand women and a hundred more.
The revered Madhusudana made that many forms, and each of those maidens thought "Madhusudana has taken my hand alone."
At night in the houses of all of them, Keshava, creator of the world, Hari, bearing universal form, stayed, Brahmins.
Aniruddha, restrained in battle, the mighty, married Usha, Bana's daughter, granddaughter of Bali, best of Brahmins,
in which a great terrible war occurred between Hari and Shankara, where Bana's thousand arms were cut by the discus-bearer.

Brahmin, how did the war occur for Usha's sake between Hara and Krishna, and how did Hari destroy Bana's arms?
brahmapuran:205:10	You ought to tell us all this fully, fortunate one; great curiosity has arisen to hear this auspicious story.
Usha, daughter of Bana, Brahmins, seeing Parvati playing with Shambhu, then herself conceived a longing; then Gauri, knower of all minds, said to that woman:
Enough of remorse; you too will play with a husband.
